pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERN

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we use correct sentences in our speech or writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech
2. respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Construct sentences using the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of... with peers,
2. Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner is able to make own sentences using appropriate language patterns correctly.
3. Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner gains confidence to recite poems before peers. Values:
4. Respect: This is promoted as the learner is able to appreciates other’s contributions when working to identify lines from the poem that have language patterns.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we use correct sentences in our speech or writing?
2. How can we write sentences correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
